paragraphs: In Sandwell the council does not run fostering itself. Sandwell Children's Trust, an independent not-for-profit company, looks after the borough's children in care, and its fostering service, Foster Sandwell, is registered with Ofsted as an independent fostering agency even though it recruits only for Sandwell's own children. The independent agencies shown above cover the borough as well. Fostering for the Trust means caring for local children with its social workers; an agency assesses, trains and supervises you itself, and the Trust's statement of purpose says that when it has no foster home of its own available, it may commission one from an independent agency.

The Trust's annual report to Ofsted for 2024-25 shows why new carers matter. On 31 March 2025 it had 156 main foster carers, 77 of them mainstream carers and 79 family and friends (connected) carers. Its mainstream households offered 128 approved places, down from 175 two years earlier, and 104 of them were filled. Ofsted inspected the service in October 2024 and judged it good. The report names the needs carers meet: children who have lived through trauma and abuse, and support for carers' own children too.

Carers can offer short-term, long-term, emergency, respite, specialist, parent and child, fostering for adoption and staying put arrangements after 18. A supervising social worker visits at least every eight weeks. The law allows eight months for an assessment, but the Trust aims to finish within 16 weeks. The Trust does not set out its rates on a page we have checked, so ask it and the agencies above what they pay.

Help is also being organised across the region. In July 2026 the government named the Black Country, with Dudley, Sandwell, Walsall and Wolverhampton, as one of four new fostering hubs, and the four have since launched it as Black Country Fostering: one point of contact for information and advice, an ambassador scheme for talking to experienced carers, and training and support for those already fostering (blackcountryfostering.org.uk, 0800 923 3706). Sandwell also led the successful bid for a West Midlands regional care co-operative of 14 councils, announced in July 2026, to improve care for the region's children, of whom about 11,560 are in care.
Foster Sandwell's number is 0800 358 0899. Speak to it and two or three of the services above, and see the Birmingham, Dudley, Walsall and Wolverhampton pages if you live near the borough's edge.
